data.note:
Reflection note:

Unblinding reveals specimen s_10190ff204 was mitoxantrone (PubChem CID 4212, CHEMBL58), annotated in BBBC021 as DNA replication and curated in ChEMBL as DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor / DNA inhibitor (e19). This matches the protocol's NSC vote of DNA replication (2/4 wells, low similarities 0.49-0.53).

Phenotypically, mitoxantrone intercalates DNA and poisons topoisomerase II, classically described as "more than just another topoisomerase II poison" (PMID 26286294) and reviewed mechanistically in PMID 3512224 and PMID 42442624. At 24h in MCF-7 we observed extreme large-nucleus (z up to 61 at 1µM, rho +0.80), multinucleate proxy (z 13-18, ~0.52-0.66 vs DMSO 0.17), loss of nuclear solidity/form factor, and cell rounding/shrinkage - features shared with Aurora inhibition via cytokinesis failure/polyploidy. Microscopist suggestions of Aurora kinase inhibitors in both high-dose and 0.1µM low-dose fields reflected this overlap: lobed/kidney-shaped hyperchromatic nuclei, bi/multinucleate cells in shared cytoplasm, consistent with topo II inhibition leading to failed chromosome segregation and endoreduplication rather than classic mitotic arrest (frac_mitotic_like rho -0.77, not elevated).

The Scientist call of Aurora kinase inhibitors was therefore phenotypically plausible but mechanistically imprecise; the protocol NSC majority over the 4 informative wells (0.1,0.3,1.0,3.0µM spanning emergence to maximal nuclear size heterogeneity) correctly recovered DNA replication despite very low cosine similarities and a split atlas neighbourhood dominated by microtubule stabilizers (7/10 neighbours, e6). This illustrates how topo II inhibitors can mimic Aurora/mitotic polyploidy phenotypes at short incubation without mitotic index increase, and why integrating dose-resolved multinucleation + nuclear solidity with low mitotic signal plus literature on mitoxantrone DNA damage is needed to discriminate DNA replication stress from direct Aurora/Eg5/microtubule

reflection.text: As Scientist I called Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.62) and was wrong; true MoA is DNA replication (mitoxantrone, DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor per e18/e19, PMID 26286294, PMID 42442624, PMID 3512224) and the blinded protocol 1-NN majority vote was correct (DNA replication 2/4 wells, summed similarity 1.013). What got right: e2-e5 quantitatively captured the phenotype driving mimicry - frac_large_nucleus z+15.0 to +61.1, frac_multinucleate_proxy z+15.3, nuc_solidity z-29.8 with rho -0.80 (e12), plus cell_roundness -12.2 to -19.1 and cell_major_axis +14.9. These are real effects of topoisomerase II poisoning leading to polyploid/enlarged irregular nuclei that phenocopy cytokinesis failure. What misled: I weighted e7 and e15 describe_phenotype both stating Aurora candidates and my integration (e16 0.65 Aurora) over e6 compare_to_reference_atlas. e6 actually voted DNA replication 2/4 (similarities 0.492 at 0.3uM and 0.521 at 0.1uM) despite k-neighbors 7/10 Microtubule stabilizers; I dismissed this as split low-similarity (0.49-0.52) and favored microscopy. I also misread e10 frac_mitotic_like rho -0.77 p=0.23 as arguing against DNA replication/microtubule arrest, when decreased mitotic entry is expected with DNA replication stress, and dismissed e13 tub_glcm_contrast rho +1.0 p=0.0 z+21.8 which was the only significant dose-response and did not fit Aurora. Acquisition choice: e1 had 8 doses 0.003-10uM budget 4 wells; I sampled 0.1,0.3,1,3uM leaving budget 0, so no replicate at 1uM (similarity 0.546 Microtubule stabilizer outlier) and no extremes where cell_count rho -0.60 (e11) cytotoxicity or stronger S-phase arrest might have separated DNA replication from Aurora. e20 returned 539 hits for topoisomerase mechanism but e21 returned 0 hits for polyploidy and I lacked literature to recognize this known mimicry at run time.
what_was_right: e2-e5 large-nucleus, multinucleation, low solidity signals were true topoisomerase II induced nuclear aberrancy
e6 NSC protocol vote correctly identified DNA replication 2/4 despite low per-well similarity
what_was_wrong: overrode e6 with e7/e15 microscopist Aurora calls
interpreted negative mitotic trend e10 as excluding DNA replication
ignored significant tubulin contrast e13 and non-significant p 0.2-0.6 trends e8-e12 e14 with n=4
reflection.next_experiment: DNA content flow >4N plus pHH3-Ser10/phospho-Aurora vs reference Aurora inhibitor and mitoxantrone to separate secondary polyploidy from primary Aurora inhibition

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

## Experiments (4 of 4 wells)

| Evidence | Dose (µM) | Replicate | Cells | Strongest changes vs DMSO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| e2 | 0.3 | 1 | 72 | frac_large_nucleus z=+15.0; act_glcm_contrast z=+13.2; cell_roundness z=-12.2 |

## Steps

1. `list_available_experiments` — List doses and budget to plan sampling strategy.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 16: Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.65, Microtubule stabilizers 0.15, DNA replication 0.08, Eg5 inhibitors 0.06, Protein synthesis 0.03, Protein degradation 0.03

## Conclusion

**Aurora kinase inhibitors** (stated probability 0.62); key evidence e2, e3, e4, e5, e7, e15, e8, e12, e10.

Why: NSC vote is split and low-similarity (DNA rep 2/4, 0.49-0.52) while quantitative and microscopy phenotypes consistently show cytokinesis failure; submitting Aurora as Scientist call with evidence.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Immunofluorescence for phospho-Aurora A/B/C and phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 plus DNA-content flow cytometry on same dose range vs reference Aurora inhibitor control; quantify polyploid >4N peak and reduction of pHH3 to separate Aurora inhibition from Eg5/microtubule stabilizer mitotic arrest.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

**APPROVE** — Evidence supports Aurora kinase inhibitors over runner-ups. Across doses 0.1–3 µM: strong large-nucleus (z=+12 to +61), multinucleation (z≈+13 to +19 at 1–3 µM), and nuclear solidity loss, with low mitotic fraction arguing against Eg5/microtubule arrest, and microscopy independently notes cytokinesis-failure morphology. Tubulin contrast (ρ=+1.0) and the split NSC vote (DNA replication 2/4, similarity 0.49–0.52; atlas k-neighbors favor Microtubule stabilizers) keep 0.62 from being higher, but DNA replication and Microtubule stabilizers do not explain the combined multinucleation/polyploid phenotype as well. Protocol call disagrees and is weak, but budget left = 0, so no affordable replicate/dose can make the NSC vote decisive.

## Unblinding

Compound: **mitoxantrone** (PubChem CID [4212](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/4212))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor; DNA inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **DNA replication**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA replication**.

## Reflection

As Scientist I called Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.62) and was wrong; true MoA is DNA replication (mitoxantrone, DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor per e18/e19, PMID 26286294, PMID 42442624, PMID 3512224) and the blinded protocol 1-NN majority vote was correct (DNA replication 2/4 wells, summed similarity 1.013). What got right: e2-e5 quantitatively captured the phenotype driving mimicry - frac_large_nucleus z+15.0 to +61.1, frac_multinucleate_proxy z+15.3, nuc_solidity z-29.8 with rho -0.80 (e12), plus cell_roundness -12.2 to -19.1 and cell_major_axis +14.9. These are real effects of topoisomerase II poisoning leading to polyploid/enlarged irregular nuclei that phenocopy cytokinesis failure. What misled: I weighted e7 and e15 describe_phenotype both stating Aurora candidates and my integration (e16 0.65 Aurora) over e6 compare_to_reference_atlas. e6 actually voted DNA replication 2/4 (similarities 0.492 at 0.3uM and 0.521 at 0.1uM) despite k-neighbors 7/10 Microtubule stabilizers; I dismissed this as split low-similarity (0.49-0.52) and favored microscopy. I also misread e10 frac_mitotic_like rho -0.77 p=0.23 as arguing against DNA replication/microtubule arrest, when decreased mitotic entry is expected with DNA replication stress, and dismissed e13 tub_glcm_contrast rho +1.0 p=0.0 z+21.8 which was the only significant dose-response and did not fit Aurora. Acquisition choice: e1 had 8 doses 0.003-10uM budget 4 wells; I sampled 0.1,0.3,1,3uM leaving budget 0, so no replicate at 1uM (similarity 0.546 Microtubule stabilizer outlier) and no extremes where cell_count rho -0.60 (e11) cytotoxicity or stronger S-phase arrest might have separated DNA replication from Aurora. e20 returned 539 hits for topoisomerase mechanism but e21 returned 0 hits for polyploidy and I lacked literature to recognize this known mimicry at run time.

What was right:
- e2-e5 large-nucleus, multinucleation, low solidity signals were true topoisomerase II induced nuclear aberrancy
- e6 NSC protocol vote correctly identified DNA replication 2/4 despite low per-well similarity

What was wrong or missed:
- overrode e6 with e7/e15 microscopist Aurora calls
- interpreted negative mitotic trend e10 as excluding DNA replication
- ignored significant tubulin contrast e13 and non-significant p 0.2-0.6 trends e8-e12 e14 with n=4

Proposed next experiment: DNA content flow >4N plus pHH3-Ser10/phospho-Aurora vs reference Aurora inhibitor and mitoxantrone to separate secondary polyploidy from primary Aurora inhibition
